directAnswer: St. Anicetus was the eleventh bishop of Rome, traditionally from Emesa in Syria and so remembered as the first Syrian pope. He is best known for receiving St. Polycarp of Smyrna, who came to Rome to discuss the date of Easter; the two disagreed but remained in full communion. The historian Hegesippus also visited Rome during his pontificate.

sections.h2: Polycarp’s Visit and the Easter Question
paras: The churches of Asia Minor celebrated the Pascha on the fourteenth day of the Jewish month of Nisan, whatever day of the week it fell, while Rome kept it on Sunday. St. Polycarp, the elderly bishop of Smyrna who had known the apostle John, traveled to Rome to discuss this and other matters with Anicetus. Irenaeus, who reports the meeting in a letter preserved by Eusebius, says neither could persuade the other to change his tradition.

Yet the two bishops parted in peace. According to Irenaeus, Anicetus yielded to Polycarp the celebration of the Eucharist in his own church as a mark of respect. Irenaeus later held up this episode as a model of unity amid differences when he urged Pope Victor I not to break communion over the same question.

Hegesippus, a Christian writer from the East, came to Rome while Anicetus was bishop and, by his own account, drew up a list of the Roman succession, noting that Eleutherus was then Anicetus’s deacon. His work survives only in fragments, but it shows how important the line of bishops already was as a guarantee of sound teaching.

The Liber Pontificalis describes Anicetus as a Syrian from Emesa and credits him with forbidding clergy to wear long hair. Later tradition honors him as a martyr, though early sources do not describe his death.

keyFacts: Eleventh bishop of Rome, c. 155 to c. 166
Traditionally from Emesa (modern Homs), Syria; called the first Syrian pope
Received St. Polycarp of Smyrna to discuss the date of Easter
Hegesippus compiled a Roman succession list during his pontificate
Honored as a martyr by later tradition

faqs.question: What happened when St. Polycarp met Pope Anicetus?
faqs.answer: They discussed the date of Easter, which Asian churches kept on the fourteenth of Nisan and Rome kept on Sunday. Neither changed his practice, but they stayed in communion, and Anicetus invited Polycarp to celebrate the Eucharist in Rome, according to St. Irenaeus.

faqs.question: Why is Anicetus called the first Syrian pope?
faqs.answer: The Liber Pontificalis says he came from Emesa in Syria. The source is late, but no earlier bishop of Rome is linked with Syria, so tradition counts him as the first.
